title: Why the standard gets missed, and what to cut

C1.rule: Mechanical, one owned file, fully specified, no design choice

C2.rule: Bounded implementation or tests, clear spec, one or two owned files and their tests

C3.rule: Cross-module design; changes a gate or the ledger contract; wrong means every project inherits it

C4.rule: Planning, merging, reconciling, anything in a project's real data, a sponsor decision

items.title: Closing an item refuses without the evidence its own done line demands
items.what: The measured cause: 9 of the 16 items whose done criterion demands a measurement were closed without performing it (finding 23/F-02, and 23/F-07 and 28/F-01 are two more of the same shape). The build half was done every time; the verification half was skipped and the item closed anyway. Nothing refuses. Make tracker set --status done read the item's own done line: when it demands a measurement -- measured, before and after, per 100, wall clock, a percentage -- the closing event must carry a number, or the close is refused with the done line quoted back. DECIDED (D1): the refusal carries --no-measurement "<reason>", and the reason is written into the log so every override stays visible.
items.done: An item whose done criterion demands a measurement cannot be closed with an event carrying no number; the refusal quotes the criterion; an item with no such criterion closes as it does today; tested against real closed items from the ledgers.

items.title: The builder's own gate runs the checks the merge gate runs
items.what: Twice today docs/workflow.html drifted behind the rules and main went red, because bin/workflow-stamp --check lives in gates.merge and a builder runs a scoped test set -- so a check that exists fires only at integration, when it is most expensive. Same shape for version-check. Put the cheap pre-checks in gates.quick too, and say in the brief template that a builder runs the quick gate before pushing.
items.done: gates.quick carries the same pre-checks as gates.merge; a branch that drifts the stamp or the version fails on the builder's own machine, not at integration; the brief template says so.

items.title: Conformance catches a project's stale skill copies
items.what: Finding 31/F-07: .claude/skills/{warmup,reheat}/SKILL.md are copies derecord keeps identical -- but only when someone runs derecord. They sat two days stale, missing the very fixes this session shipped, and Claude Code PREFERS those directory-scoped copies for files in that directory. A conformance check compares them to the source, so the card says so instead of nobody noticing.
items.done: Conformance fails when a project's skill copy differs from common-rules' source, naming the file and the fix; holds when they match or when the project keeps none.

items.title: An inventory of every rule in the must-read: enforced, moved, or cut
items.what: CLAUDE-workflow.md carries 76 prose rules against 12 machine checks, and the mandatory read is about 16,200 tokens -- 13% of a context window before any work. The rules that held today are code (parts validation, quiet's verdict, land's refusals, proposalcheck); the ones that failed are prose a session must remember (use the Read tool -- measurably failing; stage, do not set -- my own briefs broke it). Go through every rule with one of three verdicts: enforced by code, moved to reference and out of the mandatory read, or cut.
items.done: Every rule in the must-read carries a verdict and a reason; the mandatory read is measurably smaller, reported in tokens before and after; nothing enforced was lost in the move.

items.title: Deprecate and delete what has been replaced
items.what: /standard's own description says it is a shortcut for /warmup and will be removed next release -- it is still here. The Lanes block is kept folded on a page that now has four better views. tracker set --add-part cannot build parts up incrementally (30/F-01) and its only working path is the whole --parts JSON. Deprecations that never delete are how a standard gets long enough to stop being read. DECIDED (D5): /standard is NOT deleted -- the sponsor's own global CLAUDE.md instructs sessions to follow it when he types it, so removing it would break a command he uses. Remove its self-deprecation note instead. The Lanes block goes; --add-part's incremental path is fixed, not deleted.
items.done: Each deprecated mechanism is either deleted or carries a dated removal note naming its replacement; nothing points at a removed thing; the CHANGELOG entry says what went and what took its place.

items.title: quiet's verdict line cannot be fooled by an application's own output
items.what:
Reported by the PhotoVault app session as RQ-09 on its 2026-09-24 open-fix list: bin/quiet printed "FAILED · 2 failed" on a gate that was 1,522 passed and 0 failed. Exit code was right; only the printed verdict was wrong, which matters because OPERATING-RULES sends every session to read exactly that line -- a wrong verdict there is worse than none.

Two defects behind the one symptom, both reproduced before fixing. The word alternation had no trailing boundary, so `failed` matched the prefix of the app's own `failedBatches=0` and the line `found=2 failedBatches=0` read as "2 failed". And the search was unanchored and ran line by line, so the first summary-shaped fragment anywhere in the log won long before pytest printed its real summary. The app suggested anchoring with re.MULTILINE; anchoring the summary to a whole line does the same job and also covers pytest's `=` padding.
tests: an application debug line is not read as a pytest summary
a summary-shaped substring inside a line is ignored
a real failure is still a failure
zeros spelled out are still green
xfailed and deselected counts do not read as failures
items.done: A green gate prints a green verdict whatever the application under test logs, and a failing gate still prints FAILED.

log.event: filed and fixed in the same turn, from the PhotoVault app's fix list (RQ-09)
log.evidence: bin/quiet: _WORD alternation with \b boundaries and _SUMMARY anchored to a whole line, padding and duration tolerated; the counts regex got the same boundary. tests/test_quiet.py: 6 new tests, 46 passed.
